Hi Marissa / Dev team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great overview of Redwood's runtime and options. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align next steps: 

- Background: We're currently running a mix of models via OpenAI API for low-latency endpoints and a legacy on-prem GPU cluster (K8s + custom scheduler) for bulk batch jobs. We're evaluating a migration that reduces cost and simplifies ops without regressing latency or throughput.
- Primary requirements: P95 latency < 250ms for chat endpoints, predictable throughput for peak inference, support for GDPR-era data residency in the US/EU, and contract/procurement timeline inside 8 weeks.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 and audit log access are required; some PII never leaves our environment for certain workloads.

Questions:
1) For the short-term pilot, would Redwood Hosted API meet our P95 latency targets, or do you recommend Dedicated capacity right away?
2) What's the typical migration path you see for teams moving from OpenAI + self-hosted clusters?
3) Any blockers for us to run a Private VPC/on-prem eval (regulatory scope, lead time for infra setup)?

We'll share internal infra contacts and a short list of test prompts for the pilot.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Great talking with you and Priya. Below is a concise plan and my answers to your questions. Attaching our deployment options overview and a short migration playbook for reference (see attachments).

Short answers:
- Pilot recommendation: Start with a short Hosted API pilot for the low-risk endpoints (0-2M tokens/day) to validate latency and quality. If we see consistent P95 violations or need sustained capacity, move to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) as the next step.
- Typical migration path: 1) Pilot on Hosted API (validate model matching & latency); 2) Move traffic to Dedicated for predictable throughput/costs; 3) For regulated workloads, transition subset to Private VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking.
- Private VPC blockers: primarily procurement and network setup (IP allowlists, VPN/TGW, KMS access). Lead time is typically 4-8 weeks depending on procurement and infra readiness.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + test prompt list from Lumina (you)
2) Week 1: Hosted API pilot (we provide credentials + pre-configured sample prompts) — Redwood to instrument latency & cost traces
3) Week 2-3: Analyze pilot results; if P95 > 250ms or sustained QPS > dedicated sizing, scope Dedicated sizing and quote
4) Week 4-6: Procurement & Dedicated onboarding OR Private VPC kick-off (if Lumina wants to proceed directly)

Next steps I can own this week:
- Share redwood-deployment-options.pdf and migration-playbook.xlsx (attached)
- Set up a short pilot workspace and API keys for your test prompts
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up on Wed Apr 14 to review pilot metrics and procurement cadence

Subject: Technical notes: latency, KV cache, and Private VPC prerequisites

Hey Alex / team — following up with a few technical clarifications from our infra/serving side that should help set expectations for the pilot and any potential Dedicated or Private deployment.

- Hosted API latency: For most traffic profiles (seq len < 1024, model variants we discussed), P95s in-hosted regions are commonly ~150-220ms under pilot QPS. If your production QPS needs sustained concurrency, Dedicated gives more predictable P95 under heavy load because you reserve GPU pools and isolation.
- KV cache + batching: We'll enable prefix caching for repeated sessions and adaptive batching to reduce token cost while keeping tail latency stable. For migration from a self-hosted KV cache, we can provide a cache warm-up plan and a TTL strategy in the migration-playbook.xlsx.
- Data residency & Private VPC: For Private VPC/on-prem we require: (1) network peering or VPN/TGW configuration details, (2) KMS integration for customer-managed keys, (3) Egress rules for pull-based container image updates (or offline image delivery for air-gapped). Typical infra lead time is 4-8 weeks after netops procurement completes.
- Certificates & audits: If Lumina needs an in-line proxy or mTLS, we can support it; we'll need the cert chain and a test endpoint during onboarding.

I'll attach a draft SOW (internal template) for Dedicated and Private options and can tailor it once we confirm scope.

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf
